# Model card: NutriSense AI

*IDP P020 · AI Nutrition Detection and Diet Suggestion using Deep Learning · Mentor: Dr. Vivek Sharma*
*Team: Garveet Singh, Vishwas Ahuja, Chandan Kumar, Reedima (CSE) · Prerna Singh, Mehak Kamboj (Law) · Kushagra Sharma (Management)*
*Generated by `nutrisense_ml/report.py` on 2026-10-19 22:03. Every number below comes from that run.*

> **Data provenance.** All training data is **synthetic**, produced by `simulate.py` from the app's food knowledge base
> (IFCT 2017 / USDA values) and ICMR-NIN 2020 RDAs. No real users exist yet. These results show the pipeline works
> end to end and how models compare under controlled conditions; they are **not** evidence of real-world accuracy.

## 1. Nutrient-gap model
**Task.** From a person's profile and their first 3 days of logs, predict whether iron, B12, calcium,
protein and fiber will be *adequate* (≥80% of RDA), *need attention* (50–79%) or be a *higher priority* (<50%) over the next 7 days.
**Data.** 1920 train / 480 test windows, split by user (no person in both sets). 35 features.
**Selected:** `ridge_share_regression` (best grouped 3-fold CV macro-F1).

| model | CV macro-F1 | test macro-F1 | next-week intake MAE |
|---|---|---|---|
| rule_baseline | – | 0.614 | 0.1314 |
| logistic_regression | 0.611 | 0.585 | – |
| random_forest | 0.5953 | 0.603 | – |
| gradient_boosting | 0.5928 | 0.598 | – |
| neural_network_mlp | 0.5572 | 0.578 | – |
| ridge_share_regression | 0.6276 | 0.610 | 0.1031 |
| gbm_share_regression | 0.5956 | 0.594 | 0.107 |
| mlp_share_regression | 0.5642 | 0.607 | 0.1253 |

| nutrient | macro-F1 (selected) | macro-F1 (rule baseline) | accuracy (selected) |
|---|---|---|---|
| iron | 0.570 | 0.581 | 0.858 |
| b12 | 0.585 | 0.592 | 0.694 |
| calcium | 0.458 | 0.510 | 0.642 |
| protein | 0.775 | 0.756 | 0.787 |
| fiber | 0.660 | 0.630 | 0.808 |

**Reading the result honestly.** The selected model forecasts next week's intake more precisely than simply trusting the 3-day average
(MAE 0.103 vs 0.131), but after thresholding into three classes it is roughly level with the
rule baseline (macro-F1 0.610 vs 0.614). Flexible models (gradient boosting, MLP) did not help on this dataset size,
which matches the project's stated decision: model complexity is not a guarantee of accuracy.
**Vitamin D** is excluded: vitamin D is 'higher priority' for ~98% of the synthetic cohort (food alone rarely meets 15 µg); the app uses a rule + sunlight advice instead of a model.

## 2. Meal-suggestion acceptance model
**Task.** Predict whether a user accepts a suggested meal, to re-rank gap-closing suggestions.
**Data.** 69,564 train / 17,316 test impressions; features from days 0–6, labels from days 7–13; split by user.
**Selected:** `gradient_boosting` (best test ROC-AUC).

| model | ROC-AUC | log-loss | hit@1 (top pick accepted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| popularity_baseline | 0.5562 | 0.6822 | 0.474 |
| random_pick | – | – | 0.445 |
| logistic_regression | 0.6432 | 0.6542 | 0.551 |
| gradient_boosting | 0.6469 | 0.652 | 0.556 |
| neural_network_mlp | 0.6384 | 0.6569 | 0.549 |

The selected model raises the chance that the first suggestion is accepted from 44.5% (random) and
47.4% (most popular meals) to **55.6%**. Strongest signals: times_eaten, kcal_x_lose, position, goal_lose.

## 3. Food image recognition
Not trained yet. `vision/train_food_classifier.py` holds the transfer-learning setup (MobileNetV3, ImageNet weights) for the
29 plate classes the app recognises. It needs a labelled Indian food photo dataset (see `vision/README.md`).
The app's scanner currently uses curated results, as disclosed on its *How the AI works* screen.

## 4. Intended use and limits
- General nutrition guidance for healthy adults; **not** a medical device and not for diagnosis.
- Not validated for pregnancy, children, athletes or clinical conditions.
- Synthetic data cannot capture real behaviour: retrain and re-evaluate on consented real logs before any claim of accuracy.
- Fairness check needed on real data across sex, diet and region before deployment.
